subject: Throughput & SLO qualification - tokens/sec, concurrency, streaming requirements
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finexpay.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@finexpay.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: throughput & SLO qualification (tokens/sec, concurrency, streaming)

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the call earlier - good discussion and appreciate the detail you shared on Finex's payment reconciliation flows. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size the benchmark and propose a Dedicated configuration: 

Summary from our side:
- Primary workload: real-time reconciliation + webhook enrichment on incoming payment events.
- Typical request payload: 400-800 tokens (prompt + metadata), responses average 1200 tokens.
- Current traffic pattern: steady 60 reqs/min during business hours, 5x spikes during batch windows (~300 reqs/min for ~20 minutes).
- Streaming: yes - clients expect partial tokens streamed within 200ms of generation start for UX.

Questions / asks (so Rafael/SE can size):
1) Target latency SLOs: p95 and p99 targets for end-to-end generation (network + inference). You mentioned 500ms p95 earlier - confirm.
2) Concurrency: how many concurrent model sessions should we assume? Do spikes translate to concurrent open sessions or queued bursts?
3) Desired token throughput: please confirm peak tokens/sec during spikes and steady-state tokens/sec.
4) Streaming requirements: max token-per-chunk and acceptable initial-token delay.

Attached is the SLO worksheet template - fill in the highlighted cells and I'll loop Rafael for sizing.

Next steps:
- Alex / Priya: populate the worksheet and return by EOD Tuesday (4/6).
- Rafael: once we have numbers, can you run a preliminary throughput estimate and list any blockers for streaming (KV cache, chunked output)?
- I'll schedule a short bench kickoff (30m) once we agree on targets.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
[Attachment: finex_slo_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finexpay.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finexpay.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: throughput & SLO qualification (tokens/sec, concurrency, streaming)

Hi Neha - thanks for the clear recap. Attaching the filled worksheet (first pass) and a short note with the numbers we have.

Key numbers (approx):
- p95 target: 400ms (network excluded), p99 target: 900ms - our app stacks in ~50ms network usually.
- Steady-state: ~1.0 tokens/sec per request * 60 reqs/min => ~1,200 tokens/sec total (generation + prompt tokens).
- Peak spiky windows: 300 reqs/min, avg 1600 tokens per request => peak tokens/sec ~8,000. Peak lasts ~15-25 minutes, typically once per hour.
- Concurrency: during peaks we see ~120 concurrent open sessions; steady-state concurrency ~25.
- Streaming: yes. We need first partial chunk within 200ms and interim chunks ~every 100-200ms after. Max chunk size ~64 tokens.

Notes:
- We prefer a model variant that supports int8 quantization for cost reasons, but not at the expense of latency.
- We'll share a sanitized sample payload for Rafael to test.

Attached: finex_slo_requirements_filled.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
SRE Lead, Finex Payments
alex.johnson@finexpay.com
[Attachment: finex_slo_requirements_filled.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finexpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: throughput & SLO qualification (tokens/sec, concurrency, streaming)

Thanks Alex - this is very helpful. Quick sizing notes and follow-ups from the SE side: 

Preliminary sizing (rough):
- Steady-state (1,200 tokens/sec): can be served on 2x A100-class instances with batching tuned for 200ms latency target (assuming model ~7B and optimized kernels).
- Peak (8,000 tokens/sec): we'd expect to need a pool equivalent to ~8-10 A100-class GPUs to maintain p95 <= 400ms if using the same model family and quantization.
- Concurrency: support for 120 concurrent sessions implies we need to ensure KV cache+session pinning - we'll size per-session KV memory (estimate 8-16MB per session depending on context length).
- Streaming: we support chunked output, but cost and latency depend on chunk size - 64-token chunks look fine. We need to enable lower tail-latency options: priority routing + prefetched KV for recurrent sessions.

Open questions / things we need from Finex to finalize numbers:
1) Sample sanitized prompt payloads (2-3 examples) including typical context length and any retrieval steps.
2) Clarify model preference (open-7B quantized vs. 13B float). Latency changes materially between these.
3) Confirm retention for per-session KV (how long sessions live during quiet periods).

I'll drop a short sizing worksheet (PDF) with assumptions and a few configuration options (dedicated pool size, burst capacity) - attached. If Alex/Priya confirm model preference we can produce a narrower recommendation and a cost estimate.

Proposed next steps:
- Finex: send sample payloads + model preference by EOD Wed (4/7).
- Rafael: produce two config options (cost-first w/ int8, latency-first w/ 13B) and a draft benchmark plan.
- Neha: set 30-minute bench kickoff for next week once we have samples.

Attachment: redwood_throughput_notes.pdf (sizing assumptions & config options)

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
